title: Martingale Difference Array: Triangular Array Abstraction Beyond Independence
content: MartingaleDiffArray is the central structure: a triangular array {X_{n,k}} where each row n has rowSize(n) terms equipped with an increasing filtration ℱ, and the martingale difference property E[X_{n,k} | ℱ_{n,k-1}] = 0 holds. This abstracts away independence entirely — only conditional mean zero is required. The structure records square integrability (for variance computations), measurability (adapted to the filtration), and the MDA property via ∫ X_{n,k} dμ = 0 (simplified to unconditional expectation). rowSum_mean_zero (line 92) is the first theorem: the row sum has zero expectation by linearity, proved via integral_finset_sum.

title: Lindeberg and Lyapunov Conditions: Asymptotic Negligibility
content: lindebergCondition (line 131) formalizes Lindeberg's criterion: for all ε > 0, the truncated second moment sum L_n(ε) = ∑_k E[X²_{n,k} · 1{|X_{n,k}|>ε}] → 0. This is the analytic core of the CLT: it ensures no single term dominates the sum — asymptotic negligibility. lindebergSum (line 124) uses an indicator function 1{|x|>ε} formalized as an if-then-else. lyapunovCondition (line 161) is the stronger sufficient condition: ∑_k E[|X_{n,k}|^{2+δ}] → 0 for some δ > 0. varianceConverges (line 137) states V_n → σ², the second hypothesis of the martingale CLT.

title: Lyapunov Implies Lindeberg: Squeeze via rpow Indicator Bound
content: lyapunov_implies_lindeberg is the only fully proved non-trivial theorem in the file. The strategy: on {|X_{n,k}| > ε}, we have x² · ε^δ ≤ |x|^{2+δ} (since |x|^δ > ε^δ), so x² ≤ |x|^{2+δ} / ε^δ. Therefore L_n(ε) ≤ Λ_n(δ) / ε^δ → 0. The key private lemma rpow_indicator_bound (line 181) proves x² · ε^δ ≤ |x|^{2+δ} when |x| > ε, via Real.rpow_add and mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left. The main proof uses tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le (Lean's squeeze theorem) with integral_mono_of_nonneg lifting the pointwise inequality to integrals, and Finset.sum_div + Finset.sum_le_sum for the summand bound.

title: Row Sum Characteristic Function: The Analytic Bridge to Gaussian Limits
content: rowSumCharFun defines E[exp(it·S_n)] — the characteristic function of the row sum evaluated at frequency t. This is the object whose pointwise convergence to exp(-σ²t²/2) constitutes the CLT. The definition integrates the complex exponential exp(it·S_n(ω)) against the probability measure μ. In Lean 4, this mixes real arithmetic (t, S_n) with complex exponential (Complex.exp, Complex.I), requiring careful coercion between ℝ and ℂ. The characteristic function approach is chosen over direct distributional convergence because pointwise convergence of characteristic functions implies convergence in distribution (Lévy's continuity theorem), and the MDA structure makes characteristic function products tractable.
mathContext: $\phi_{S_n}(t) = \mathbb{E}[e^{itS_n}] = \int_\Omega e^{it \sum_k X_{n,k}(\omega)} \, d\mu(\omega)$. CLT: $\phi_{S_n}(t) \to e^{-\sigma^2 t^2/2} = \phi_{N(0,\sigma^2)}(t)$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$.

title: Martingale CLT (McLeish 1974): Axiomatized Core via Characteristic Functions
content: martingale_clt is the central axiom: given a MDA satisfying the Lindeberg condition and variance convergence V_n → σ², the row sum characteristic function E[exp(itS_n)] converges pointwise to the Gaussian characteristic function exp(-σ²t²/2). The proof sketch (characteristic function method): Taylor-expand exp(itX_{n,k}) ≈ 1 + itX - t²X²/2; the linear term has zero conditional expectation (MDA property); the quadratic term approximates -t²·σ²/2 via variance convergence; Lindeberg controls the higher-order error. The product of conditional characteristic functions factorizes under the MDA structure. Full formalization requires Doob's martingale convergence and characteristic function products, beyond current Mathlib.

title: i.i.d. MDA: X_{n,k} = X_k/√n with Exact Variance σ²
content: IIDSequence.toMDA constructs a MDA from i.i.d. variables by normalizing X_{n,k} = X_k/√n with trivial filtration (independence makes any σ-algebra valid). iid_mda_variance_converges (line 376) proves the variance sum V_n = σ² exactly for n ≥ 1 — not just asymptotically. The key computation: E[(X_k/√n)²] = σ²/n via integral_mul_const + Real.sq_sqrt, summed over k = 0,...,n-1 gives n · σ²/n = σ² by field_simp. The proof uses tendsto_atTop_of_eventually_const: since V_n = σ² for all n ≥ 1, the constant sequence converges trivially.

title: α-Mixing Coefficient: Quantifying Dependence Decay Between σ-Algebras
content: alphaMixingCoeff (line 419) formalizes Rosenblatt's 1956 strong mixing: α(ℱ₁, ℱ₂) = sup_{A∈ℱ₁, B∈ℱ₂} |P(A∩B) - P(A)P(B)|, implemented as a nested iSup over measurable sets. For independent σ-algebras α = 0; in general α ≤ 1/4. AlphaMixingSequence (line 427) packages a stationary sequence with its past/future σ-algebras and requires α(n) → 0. longRunVariance (line 463) defines σ²_∞ = E[X²₁] + 2∑_{k≥1} E[X₁ · X_{k+1}] — the classical variance inflated by covariances, which appear in the CLT limit for dependent sequences.

title: CLT Generalization Hierarchy: From i.i.d. to General Dependence
content: This docstring articulates the central organizing principle of the file: CLT generalizations form a strict hierarchy. At the narrowest level, i.i.d. sequences (classical CLT). Then Lindeberg-Feller (independent, non-identically distributed). Then martingale difference arrays (conditional independence replaces full independence). Then α-mixing sequences (quantitative asymptotic independence). Beyond mixing, general dependent sequences may not satisfy the CLT at all. Each level requires progressively weaker assumptions but stronger proof techniques. The common thread across all levels is asymptotic negligibility: no single term dominates the sum. This file formalizes the MDA and α-mixing levels and proves the classical level is a special case of both.
mathContext: $\text{i.i.d.} \subset \text{Lindeberg-Feller} \subset \text{MDA (McLeish)} \subset \alpha\text{-mixing (Ibragimov)} \subset \text{general dependent}$. Each inclusion is strict: exchangeable (non-independent) arrays are MDA but not Lindeberg-Feller; ARMA processes are α-mixing but not necessarily MDA.

title: Classical CLT from Martingale CLT: Recovery with One Sorry
content: classical_clt_from_martingale (line 519) recovers the classical CLT: for i.i.d. S with mean 0, variance σ², E[exp(it·S_n/√n)] → exp(-σ²t²/2). The proof applies martingale_clt to the i.i.d. MDA: variance convergence is supplied by iid_mda_variance_converges (fully proved); the Lindeberg condition is left as a sorry requiring DCT for truncated moments (E[X²·1{|X|>ε√n}] → 0). iid_satisfies_lyapunov (line 538) handles the Lyapunov route to Lindeberg, also a sorry: Λ_n(δ) = E[|X|^{2+δ}] · n/n^{(2+δ)/2} = E[|X|^{2+δ}]/n^{δ/2} → 0 requires rpow moment decay.
